summary: No request waited >= 100 ms in the queue.

supporting_events.statement: queue wait p95 across requests with a queue span
max requests waiting in vLLM's queue per step

assumptions: queue wait is the time from add_request to the first engine step that scheduled the request (in-process scheduler), or vLLM's own queued_time for finished requests
the threshold separates ordinary scheduling delay from overload for this workload
competing_explanations: load-generator lateness rather than scheduler queueing (compare manifest arrival delays with the queue spans)
requests waited for KV-cache blocks rather than for step capacity (see kv_cache_pressure)
one large prefill chunk consumed the step's token budget (see long_prompt_interference)
confidence_limits: queue wait is step-granular (resolved to the end of the step that first scheduled the request)
vLLM's queued_time carries no request ids, so affected requests come only from in-process queue spans

summary: 38 request(s) decoded or waited in 18 step(s) that also prefilled a chunk > 128 tokens; those steps took 7.3 ms vs 2.8 ms for the rest. They waited while the scheduler spent its token budget on other work.

supporting_events.statement: engine steps carrying a prefill chunk above the threshold
median duration of all other steps
requests that shared such a step without owning the chunk

assumptions: an engine step's duration is set mainly by the largest prefill chunk it carries
every request scheduled in a step waits for the whole step, so sharing a long step delays its tokens
competing_explanations: the long steps were slow for another reason: first-time batch shapes or CUDA-graph capture (see warm-up in the manifest), host stalls (see host_overhead), or the tracer's own drains (see tracer_observer_effect)
the sharing requests' TTFT came from queue wait before they were scheduled, not from the step they shared (compare their queue spans)
confidence_limits: this is co-occurrence of step membership and step duration; cause is established only by the replay with long_prefill_token_threshold changed
GPU step spans, when present, show the step was GPU compute but not whose tokens consumed it
suggested_experiment: Replay with long_prefill_token_threshold set to a smaller per-step chunk (e.g. 256) and compare the sharing requests' TTFT p95 and worst inter-token stall against the long requests' TTFT cost.

summary: KV-cache usage reached 100% in 1547 step(s) with 56 preemption(s) reported by vLLM.
missing_evidence: which requests were preempted (vLLM stats carry no request ids)
assumptions: KV-cache usage at or above the threshold means block allocation can fail for new tokens
preemptions reported by vLLM in the same run are caused by that shortage
competing_explanations: high usage without preemptions is ordinary steady state for a full batch (not a problem by itself)
preemptions can also follow priority scheduling or a request longer than max_model_len allows
confidence_limits: vLLM stats carry no request ids: the requests alive during high-usage steps are known only with batch metadata
usage is sampled once per step; a shortage inside a step is not visible
suggested_experiment: Replay with a lower max_num_seqs or a higher gpu_memory_utilization and compare preemptions, KV usage max and the affected requests' TPOT.

summary: Host-side time is 21% of a typical step; steps are GPU-bound.

supporting_events.statement: median share of step time not spanned by the GPU
steps with a resolved GPU span

missing_evidence: GPU busy time (CUPTI); the CUDA-event span includes launch gaps
assumptions: host_step_ms - gpu_span_ms is time the GPU stream was not spanned by the model forward (scheduling, input preparation, output processing, tracing)
competing_explanations: the span excludes work on vLLM's other streams and includes launch gaps inside the span, so a high host share on a tiny model can be launch-bound GPU idle time rather than host work (Nsight cross-check: decode steps of a 125M model were 58% busy inside the span)
confidence_limits: measured only with UniProcExecutor on the blocking execute path; the tracer's own per-step cost is inside the host share

summary: No engine step overlapping a tracer drain was unusually long.
assumptions: a collector drain that overlaps an engine step and is a material part of that step's excess over the median delayed it
competing_explanations: the overlapping step was long for its own reasons (a large prefill chunk, a first-time shape)
confidence_limits: the drain's duration is measured by the collector thread; GIL contention it caused inside the step is inferred, not measured
